Topic: CSCI-549: Seminar in Languages and Tools. This catalog entry has student-, instructor-, or term-specific content. Create a rigorous orientation companion that teaches the stable process, standards, planning methods, evaluation criteria, and representative examples without inventing a fixed RIT syllabus. Official catalog description: This course examines current topics in Languages and Tools. This is intended to allow faculty to pilot potential new undergraduate offerings. Specific course details (such as prerequisites, course seminar, format, learning outcomes, assessment methods, and resource needs) will be determined by the faculty member(s) who propose a specific seminar course in this area. Specific course instances will be identified as belonging to the Languages and Tools cluster, the Security cluster, or both clusters. Contact Hours: Lecture 3 Regeneration revision 2: use ten distinct, specific beat titles and avoid repeating any title or section label.

Source excerpts:

[llvm-language-reference]
LLVM IR is a typed, SSA-based intermediate representation with explicit instructions, basic blocks, functions, memory operations, and control flow. A module contains global values, functions, declarations, and metadata. A function contains basic blocks, and every basic block ends with a terminator instruction. Phi instructions select values according to the predecessor control-flow edge. Load and store instructions make memory access explicit. Valid IR must satisfy structural and typing rules. The verifier reports IR that violates those rules. Compiler work separates parsing and semantic analysis from lowering, verification, optimization, and target-specific code generation.

[python-language-reference]
The Python language reference specifies lexical analysis, data model behavior, execution, expressions, statements, functions, classes, exceptions, and module import semantics. Python objects have identity, a type, and a value. Names are bound to objects within namespaces and scopes. Expressions produce values, while statements control execution and bindings. Exceptions interrupt normal control flow until a matching handler processes them or they propagate. The import system searches for modules and binds loaded modules into a namespace. Programs should be reasoned about through explicit state, control flow, data representation, contracts, tests, and observable behavior. Debugging separates syntax, runtime, and logical failures, while decomposition and abstraction reduce the number of interacting concerns.

[rit-csci-549]
This course examines current topics in Languages and Tools. This is intended to allow faculty to pilot potential new undergraduate offerings. Specific course details (such as prerequisites, course seminar, format, learning outcomes, assessment methods, and resource needs) will be determined by the faculty member(s) who propose a specific seminar course in this area. Specific course instances will be identified as belonging to the Languages and Tools cluster, the Security cluster, or both clusters. Contact Hours: Lecture 3

beats.claim: CSCI-549 serves as a faculty pilot course to examine current topics in Languages and Tools.
beats.example: A department head proposes a new undergraduate offering focused on compiler design.
beats.title: Course Scope and Faculty Pilot Framework
beats.visualDirection: Display a flowchart showing faculty proposal -> pilot course -> cluster classification (Languages and Tools or Security).

beats.claim: Specific course instances are identified as belonging to the Languages and Tools cluster, the Security cluster, or both clusters.
beats.example: A proposed seminar on memory safety analysis is classified under both clusters.
beats.title: Cluster Classification System
beats.visualDirection: Show a Venn diagram with two overlapping circles labeled 'Languages and Tools' and 'Security', with a course title in the intersection.

beats.claim: The Python language reference specifies lexical analysis, data model behavior, execution, expressions, statements, functions, classes, exceptions, and module import semantics.
beats.example: A reference document outlines how Python handles variable binding and exception propagation.
beats.title: Language Reference Structure
beats.visualDirection: List the specified reference components in a hierarchical outline format.

beats.claim: Python objects have identity, a type, and a value, while names are bound to objects within namespaces and scopes.
beats.example: A function call binds the parameter name to a specific object instance in the local scope.
beats.title: Object Model and Namespaces
beats.visualDirection: Illustrate a namespace tree with nested scopes and object references pointing to shared memory addresses.

beats.claim: Expressions produce values, while statements control execution and bindings, and exceptions interrupt normal control flow until a matching handler processes them or they propagate.
beats.example: A division by zero triggers an exception that jumps to a try-except block.
beats.title: Control Flow and Exceptions
beats.visualDirection: Draw a control flow graph with a normal path and an exception path branching to a handler node.

beats.claim: LLVM IR is a typed, SSA-based intermediate representation with explicit instructions, basic blocks, functions, memory operations, and control flow.
beats.example: A compiler translates a high-level loop into a sequence of LLVM IR basic blocks with phi nodes.
beats.title: LLVM Intermediate Representation
beats.visualDirection: Render a simplified LLVM IR module showing a function, basic blocks, and a phi instruction at a merge point.

beats.claim: Phi instructions select values according to the predecessor control-flow edge, ensuring single static assignment form is maintained.
beats.example: A phi node chooses between two loop iteration values based on whether the loop condition was true or false.
beats.title: Phi Instructions and Control Flow
beats.visualDirection: Show a control flow graph with two incoming edges to a block containing a phi instruction that selects between two values.

beats.claim: Load and store instructions make memory access explicit, and valid IR must satisfy structural and typing rules, with the verifier reporting IR that violates those rules.
beats.example: The verifier rejects an IR module where a store instruction targets an untyped memory location.
beats.title: Memory Operations and Verification
beats.visualDirection: Display a before-and-after comparison of invalid IR (with a type mismatch) and valid IR (with explicit memory types).

beats.claim: Compiler work separates parsing and semantic analysis from lowering, verification, optimization, and target-specific code generation.
beats.example: A frontend parser generates ASTs, while a backend optimizer restructures the IR for a specific CPU architecture.
beats.title: Compiler Phase Separation
beats.visualDirection: Present a linear pipeline diagram with distinct stages: Parsing -> Semantic Analysis -> Lowering -> Verification -> Optimization -> Code Generation.

beats.claim: Faculty must evaluate proposed seminar courses against stable process standards, planning methods, and assessment criteria to ensure alignment with the Languages and Tools cluster.
beats.example: A review checklist verifies that the proposed course includes defined learning outcomes, assessment methods, and resource needs.
beats.title: Practical Analysis Checklist
beats.visualDirection: Show a checklist template with checkboxes for prerequisites, format, learning outcomes, assessment methods, and resource needs.
